skill.name: chrome-webstore-release-blueprint
skill.description: Set up Chrome Web Store API release automation with OAuth, secret handling, version checks, publishing, and submission status reporting.
skill.summary: A guided blueprint for secure, version-aware Chrome Web Store publishing workflows.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: The static matches are false positives because they identify Markdown examples, official documentation URLs, and a stated secret-file convention rather than executable behavior. The guide contains one confirmed high-severity credential-handling issue because it asks users to paste OAuth secrets into the agent conversation.

remediation.issue: The guide asks users to paste CWS_CLIENT_SECRET and CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN into the agent conversation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove those prompts and instruct users to enter credentials directly into approved local or CI secret storage. Use placeholders and verify only variable presence or masked output.

remediation.issue: The proposed GitHub secret upload helper could receive highly privileged publishing credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, least-privilege repository permissions, a dry run, masked logs, and an audit of the destination repository before uploading any secret.

remediation.issue: The workflow blueprint can publish an extension after a version change.
remediation.suggestion: Add a protected environment or manual approval before production publish, and validate the package, manifest, target item, and workflow identity before submission.

semantic_findings.description: The guide asks users to paste the OAuth client secret and refresh token into the agent conversation. Chat transcripts or agent context may expose these credentials, enabling unauthorized token use or Chrome Web Store actions.

content.user_title: Automate Chrome Web Store Releases Safely
content.value_statement: Chrome extension publishing requires careful OAuth setup, secret storage, version checks, and status tracking. This skill provides a guided workflow for configuring and verifying those release steps.
actual_capabilities: Guide Google Cloud API enablement and OAuth consent configuration.
Walk through creating Chrome Web Store OAuth credentials and refresh tokens.
Define local and CI secret names for Chrome Web Store publishing.
Design version comparison, package upload, publish, and polling workflows.
Specify a submission status checker with normalized release fields.
limitations: It cannot access Google dashboards or complete OAuth actions on the user’s behalf.
It does not create repository files unless the user requests implementation in an available repository.
It cannot verify publisher permissions, account ownership, or API responses without user-provided results.
It does not replace review of secret storage, workflow permissions, or packaged extension contents.

use_cases.title: Set Up First-Time Publishing
use_cases.description: Follow a guided checklist for enabling the API, configuring OAuth, capturing store identifiers, and preparing secrets.
use_cases.target_user: Extension developer preparing a first automated release

use_cases.title: Add Version-Gated CI Releases
use_cases.description: Design a workflow that compares versions, packages the extension, uploads changes, and avoids redundant submissions.
use_cases.target_user: DevOps engineer maintaining GitHub Actions automation

use_cases.title: Diagnose Submission Status
use_cases.description: Plan a status checker that reports published and submitted versions, review state, and common authentication failures.
use_cases.target_user: Support engineer investigating a Chrome Web Store release

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Setup Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through setting up Chrome Web Store API publishing for my extension. Ask for one detail at a time, explain where each value comes from, and pause before every credential step.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has never configured Chrome Web Store OAuth or publishing automation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI Secrets
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secret-management checklist for my GitHub Actions release workflow. Use placeholders only, identify which values belong in repository secrets, and include a dry-run verification plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a repeatable CI setup without placing credentials in repository files.

prompt_templates.title: Design Version-Gated Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Chrome Web Store release workflow that reads the manifest version, compares the published version, builds the package, uploads only when needed, polls asynchronous state, and reports submission results.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants automated publishing that avoids duplicate submissions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Release Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed Chrome Web Store release process for credential exposure, excessive workflow permissions, version mismatches, unsafe secret handling, and incomplete failure reporting. Return prioritized findings and concrete fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced engineer is reviewing an existing release design before production use.

output_examples.input: We need to publish an extension from GitHub Actions only when its version changes.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan with manifest version comparison, package creation, OAuth token exchange, status checks, conditional upload, asynchronous polling, and publish confirmation.

output_examples.input: The submission checker says the extension is not current.
output: Compare the local manifest version with the published and submitted versions.
Check whether the submission is pending review or blocked by permissions.
Inspect authentication errors and package metadata before retrying.

output_examples.input: I need to configure OAuth without exposing credentials.
output_examples.output: A placeholder-based setup checklist that keeps real values in approved secret storage and requires explicit confirmation before each sensitive step.

best_practices: Use placeholders in documentation and store real credentials only in approved local or CI secret storage.
Compare extension versions before packaging or publishing to prevent duplicate submissions.
Require explicit confirmation for dashboard actions and report authentication or permission failures clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not paste client secrets or refresh tokens into an agent conversation.
Do not commit environment files, credentials, or hardcoded secrets to the repository.
Do not publish every push without version checks, dry-run support, and permission review.

faq.question: Does this skill publish my extension automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow blueprint and asks for confirmation before user-driven dashboard or credential actions.

faq.question: Which credentials are needed?
faq.answer: The workflow uses an OAuth client ID, client secret, refresh token, publisher ID, and extension item ID.

faq.question: Where should real credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Use a protected local secret store or CI repository secrets. Never commit credentials or place them in workflow source.

faq.question: How does version gating work?
faq.answer: The workflow compares the local extension version with the published version and skips publishing when they match.

faq.question: Can this handle pending review states?
faq.answer: Yes. The blueprint includes status polling and recognizes pending review, published, tester, and staged states.

faq.question: What should I do after a 403 response?
faq.answer: Check that the authenticated account has publisher permission for the extension and that the identifiers match the intended item.
